question: Refer to the exhibit. Server1 is connected to a Cisco Nexus 9000 Series Switch via a 1-Gb port channel. The storm control is applied to the Eth0 device with a zero percent value. What does the switch do to traffic that traverses the switch interfaces during the streaming window that exceeds the bandwidth of the interfaces?
context: Exhibit: Server1, Eth0 interface bandwidth graph showing a streaming window between roughly 10-60 seconds where bandwidth peaks around 1600-1700 MB then fluctuates between 1000-1400 MB.
options: drops all of the excess traffic
theory: Traffic storm control measures the percentage of broadcast, multicast, or unknown-unicast traffic arriving during each one-second interval and drops all such traffic above the configured ceiling until the interval resets. Setting the storm-control level to zero percent sets that ceiling to zero, so any traffic of the monitored type during the interval immediately exceeds the threshold and gets suppressed entirely for that interval, rather than being partially rate-limited or fully forwarded — which is why a zero percent value results in complete suppression during high-traffic streaming windows. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 4 — Traffic Storm Control Thresholds)
